# Compliance {.unnumbered}

Compliance content consolidated in July 2026. What was a seven-section tree is
now two destinations and one remaining analysis section:

## Where compliance lives now

- **[The Federal Compliance AAN Series](../federal-aan-series/index.qmd)** —
  the compliance *offering*: a ten-volume, 58-book FedRAMP Moderate program
  covering mandates, controls, evidence, policy, incident response, training,
  and authorization — engine-neutral by design, speaking to the open
  [Evidence & Authorization Contract](../federal-aan-series/AAN_Evidence_Contract_Spec.md).
- **[UIAO — Reference Engine for the Federal Compliance AAN Series](../uiao-aan-integration/index.qmd)**
  — the engine-side companion volume: how one conformant engine satisfies the
  contract, including the engine's own compliance documentation (Books 09–14:
  control mapping & gap analysis, the SCuBA pipeline spec and value
  proposition, the NIST/FICAM crosswalk, the master document specification,
  and FedRAMP/CISA enhancement recommendations). Old
  `compliance/…` URLs redirect there.

The boundary analyses completed the consolidation in Phase 3-B: **[B. Boundary +
Authorization](../federal-aan-series/boundary/index.qmd)** — the GCC-Moderate
boundary model and analyses (B.1–B.1.3) — now lives inside the series, made
engine-neutral like the rest of the corpus, with its B.1.3 fix-coverage matrix
still drift-gated from the canon telemetry-gaps SSOT.

## Canonical invariants (unchanged)

- **Boundary:** GCC-Moderate SaaS. The only Commercial-Cloud exception is
  Amazon Connect Contact Center.
- **Evidence:** every control assertion has a signed, provenanced artifact
  behind it. No verbal assurances.
- **Classification:** Controlled · CUI · (future) Secret. "UNCLASSIFIED"
  is non-canonical and treated as drift.
- **Boundary enforcement:** out-of-scope references are rejected at canon
  validation, not at assessment time.
